hero.headline: Your child disagrees — but stays quiet because they're afraid of a fight?
hero.subheadline: "It'll cause a conflict", "they'll be offended", "a fight will start". So they either silently agree or snap — and a fight really does break out. Because there's no other way to say it.

media.alt: A child staying silent, not daring to say they think differently

pain.title: Disagreement isn't a fight
pain.body:
Your child disagrees — but is afraid to say so. Because "it'll cause a conflict", "they'll be offended", "a fight will start". At school, with friends, at home. They either stay quiet and go along with it, or speak sharply — and a fight really does break out.

But disagreement isn't a fight. It's not about thinking differently — it's about how it's said. Without the skill, any "no" sounds like an attack and triggers conflict. With no alternative, the child picks either silence or sharpness.

The result — either their position simply isn't there, or the relationship suffers. Not because they're avoiding things, but because they have no way to say "I think differently" without it landing like a blow.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
